page_title: Build a simple Twitter Bot with Node.js Part 2: DO MORE

summary.title: Build a simple Twitter Bot with Node.js Part 2: DO MORE
summary.one_liner: You learn how to turn a Twitter like-bot into a follow-bot by reusing the search loop and swapping in the friendships/create POST route from the Twitter REST API.
keywords: modify twitter bot to follow users
takeaways: Every POST call in the npm Twitter package follows the pattern T.post(route, params, callback), so the API docs give you the route and parameters.
To follow users, reuse the search loop from the first tutorial and call T.post('friendships/create', {screen_name}, callback) for each tweet's author.
Check err in the callback to log failures, and log a success message otherwise.
Changing the route and parameters is enough to turn the favorite bot into a follow bot; the rest of the code stays the same.
summary.summary: This Node.js tutorial is a follow-up to a 38-line Twitter bot that searches tweets and likes them. It explains that the Twitter REST API has many POST routes (favorites/destroy, direct_message/new, lists/create, friendships/create and more), and that each one uses the same pattern with a route, a parameters object and a callback. The author copies app.js to follow.js, keeps the search loop, and replaces the favorite call with friendships/create using the screen_name from each tweet's user, with error logging in the callback. The post is short and practical, with code snippets and a link to a GitHub repository.
